routes.title: How does a boundary become a warranted measurement?
routes.description: From the boundary primitive through observability, certification, reconstruction, and deliberate failure.

routes.title: How can health be stated as a prospective mathematical property?
routes.description: From formal Health to contextual transport, information sufficiency, finite forest provenance, data-anchored testing, and constitutive observability under maintained measurement.

items.title: The Question Behind Our Research
items.summary: Why biology, fluid dynamics, mathematical physics, formal proof, and measurement engineering keep meeting inside one long-running question about a scale-agnostic definition of health.

items.title: The boundary comes first
items.summary: Why measurement begins with the edge that makes an aggregate distinguishable, and how a maintained gradient connects boundary to health.

items.title: Fixedness
items.summary: What must remain invariant for a changing system to remain itself, and how measurement keeps hold of identity through transformation.

items.title: Algebra before AI
items.summary: Why formal structure, admissibility, and claim authority have to exist before learned inference is allowed to act.

items.title: Reading the living boundary
items.summary: A relational account of gradients, exchange, laminarity, reconstruction, and what an instrument can learn from a living surface.

items.title: Residue and residual
items.summary: Two different remainders: what a living boundary retains, and what remains after a model has been tested against a law.
A reflection on relational measurement, compression, identity, and what arithmetic hides when relationships carry the information.

items.title: What is genuinely new, precisely.
items.summary: A proof-checked living algebra of physical observables, situated carefully against the fields nearest to it.

items.title: A boundary-observable certification algebra
items.summary: How mathematical freedom is progressively admitted through physical consistency, closure, witness, and evidentiary maturity.

items.title: The temperament of a bespoke algebra
items.summary: What repeated behavior under proof reveals about the character of a mathematical object built for measurement.

items.title: The making of an observable
items.summary: How calibration, reconstruction, residual analysis, transport preservation, and claim maturity turn a signal into an observable.

items.title: How we try to make the signal fail
items.summary: Why deliberate deletion, failure tests, and longitudinal challenge belong inside the evidence chain before a relationship is allowed to count.

items.title: Constitutive Continuation Capacity
items.subtitle: A machine-checked framework for prospective health.
items.summary: Prospective health is formalized as present realization together with requirement-adequate continuation capacity, with exact lawful/viable response semantics, a requirement-visible capacity quotient and universal property, explicit query relativity, qualified presentation invariance, and robustness and measurement-sufficiency boundaries.

items.title: Prospective Health Across Contexts
items.subtitle: Contextual Licensing, Developmental Transport, and Open-System Support.
items.summary: Paper II transports the prospective-health architecture across changing contexts, developmental stages, and open-system support by separating raw capacity transport, health-visible quotient transport, and full health truth, with exact determinacy, obstruction, branching, coalescence, and support-dependence results.

items.title: Representation Sufficiency in Prospective Health
items.subtitle: Query-Visible Quotients, Transport, and Enriched Response Semantics.
items.summary: Paper III characterizes representation sufficiency for declared prospective-health queries. Sufficient representations refine the canonical query-visible quotient, which is the coarsest sufficient target for exact deterministic transport. The paper establishes the full-health observation criterion and response-grounded realizations for control, viable cost, probability, route structure, and failure-aware robustness.

items.title: Information Provenance and Conservative Enrichment in Prospective Health
items.subtitle: A Machine-Checked Finite Forest Benchmark.
items.summary: Paper IV establishes a five-state, machine-checked forest benchmark with two equivalent history encodings, an exact candidate-to-lawful-to-viable response census, and a complete distinction-loss classification across detailed capacity, coarse capacity, and declared Health. A generic conservative-refinement lemma and a strict forest example demonstrate preservation of established Health judgments under exact projection.

items.title: Constitutive Observability and the Measurement of Prospective Health
items.subtitle: State Identification and Prospective Health under Maintenance Constraints.
items.summary: Paper VI studies the measurement of present organizational state and the preservation of prospective Health under intervention in a fully defined two-site exchange system. Two presently indistinguishable states have different common-future viability. Exact observation fibers, a heterogeneous flux-readout probe and a fixed-drive repeated-cost alternative give model-relative maintaining and verdict-preserving identification, with quantified local uncertainty bounds. Continuous-time counterexamples show why sampled measurements can miss intermediate maintenance failures. Physical calibration and prospective physiological validation remain open.

items.title: Prospective Health under Declared Specifications
items.subtitle: An Auditable Empirical-Synthetic Forest Measurement Study.
items.summary: Paper V evaluates prospective Health as a model-conditional stochastic measurement using longitudinal Harvard Forest observations and synthetic benchmark worlds. It audits latent-state reconstruction, demographic calibration, query-relative representation and decision reliability; independent adult-mortality observations reveal severe hemlock-specific predictive miscalibration. The study does not establish operational forest Health.
